title: HR Administrator
description:
Sewell Wallis is looking for an HR Administrator to join a professional services business, based on-site just near Wetherby.

It is not necessary that you have a CIPD qualification, but that would benefit an application. This role would suit someone who is keen to progress, learn and get stuck into the business; you ll have a positive can-do attitude and work closely with the HR director day-to-day.

Responsibilities include supporting employee relations and case management, maintaining accurate HR records and systems, processing contracts and leavers, and ensuring compliance with employment legislation and data protection requirements.

- Employee Relations: Provide administrative support for employee relations matters, including disciplinary, grievance and performance cases, arranging meetings, preparing documentation, taking accurate notes and maintaining confidential records.
- Recruitment: Support the end-to-end recruitment process, including preparing job adverts, screening applications, coordinating interviews, communicating with candidates and supporting hiring managers.

- Employee Support: Act as a first point of contact for routine HR queries, providing support to employees and managers regarding HR processes, policies, pay, benefits and employment documentation.
- Training & Compliance: Coordinate training and e-learning activities, support performance and absence management, maintain HR policies and job descriptions, and assist with health and safety and compliance activities.
- Payroll & Benefits: Support payroll, benefits, salary reviews and employee changes by providing accurate information, preparing documentation and liaising with relevant internal teams.
- Reporting & Data Protection: Prepare HR reports and metrics, maintain effective filing and document retention systems, and ensure HR processes and records comply with data protection, confidentiality and internal policies.

What skills are we looking for?
- Confident written and verbal communication skills, with a friendly, professional and approachable manner.
- Experience working within an HR or business administration setting.
- Strong organisational and administrative abilities, with excellent attention to detail.
- A basic understanding of UK employment law and HR policies.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Outlook, Word and Excel.
- The ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
- Experience assisting with or coordinating meetings, especially those relating to employee relations.
- Currently studying towards, holding, or interested in pursuing a CIPD Level 3 qualification.
- Based locally to the office and able to travel independently using your own transport.

What's on offer?
- £28,000 - £30,000 starting salary
- 20 days annual leave plus 8 statutory bank holidays, with the addition of Christmas shutdown and your birthday off!
- Company pension scheme
- Company sick pay
- Parking available

description: An opportunity has arisen for a confident and supportive administrator to join our busy and dedicated Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment team (CRHT) based at The Orchards in Ripon. This post is part-time, 34hours per week, Monday to Friday. The CRHT team operates 24-hours a day, providing advice and support to those seeking help in a mental health emergency or being referred by a healthcare professional for assessment and triage. Further information about our services can be found here CRHT services provided by TEWV The Orchards is a base of operations for multiple mental health teams working across North Yorkshire, County Durham and Teesside. The CRHT team are based here, as are the Early Intervention Psychosis team and there is an inpatient mental health recovery unit on site too. The site benefits from free parking and is easily accessible by car and bicycle. As a member of the CRHT team, you will work in an open plan office alongside clinicians and support staff. The office is an area of high activity, and no two days are the same. If you are looking for a new challenge, enjoy variety in your work and are looking to be part of a team striving to make a difference, we will welcome your application for this role. Please do consider making contact with the recruiting manager for an informal conversation prior to submitting an application, we'd like to hear from you . Whilst having extensive experience in an administrative role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is not. We are first and foremost looking for an individual with a passion for people, customer service experience, extensive organisational and digital data management skills, an interest in working in a health care setting and a 'can do' attitude. This role is at the heart of a cohesive and dedicated team and is a pivotal role in the day-to-day operations. You will work collaboratively with other administrators, closely with the clinicians and the team manager, to support them in ensuring high standards are maintained and that they have everything they need to provide the best possible care for service users. The successful candidate will be able to evidence that they are comfortable multi-tasking, are confident offering supervisory support to other administrative staff, can communicate confidently, build strong working relationships with a variety of people and can prioritise their workload. Duties will include comprehensive, pro-active and re-active diary management for the Consultants and medical team; processing of digital dictation and production of patient letters; minute taking; accurate and timely record keeping (confidential, sensitive and legal information) on the electronic patient record system. For full details please refer to the Job Description. For guidance on the application process, please refer to the TRAC helpful hints attached. With a starting salary of £28,392 per annum (pro-rata), a generous NHS pension scheme, a fantastic annual leave package (27 days annual leave plus bank holidays) and access to other NHS staff benefits and discounts, it is fair to say that this job has a lot to offer. And, its not just the NHS pay scale and benefits that we offer that make joining our organisation an excellent choice, there are many training and development opportunities available, giving you the opportunity for career progression. All staff have regular 1-2-1s, quarterly supervision meetings and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for discussion around achievements, challenges and aspirations. Staff recognition is very important to us; we work closely with colleagues to support development, the staff voice, and to recognise teams and individuals through our Greatix and Star Award schemes; highlighting the outstanding work being done every day. We recognise that Administrators are professionals and are a valuable asset to our organisation. We understand that they have a key role in the support and delivery of our services and that their contribution helps us in achieving our aim of consistently providing safe and high quality care for our service users. The kind of care we would want for ourselves and for our loved ones.
